title: The secret mud on every baseball
hook: Every Major League baseball is rubbed with mud from a secret New Jersey riverbank.
peek: New baseballs are too shiny to grip. Since 1938 the fix has been a fine mud from a spot in New Jersey that only one family knows. Before each game, umpire staff rub it into every ball.
lede: A new baseball has a slick, glossy surface that pitchers struggle to grip. In 1938 Lena Blackburne, a coach for the Philadelphia Athletics, went looking for something better than the water and dirt used then. He found a smooth mud near his home in New Jersey, by a tributary of the Delaware River. Major League Baseball has used his mud ever since.

bullets.text: The product still carries his name. Blackburne passed the secret to a friend, and that family has run the business since, digging the mud themselves and keeping the exact spot private.
The mud is very fine, often compared to chocolate pudding or cold cream. Rubbed in with a little water, it takes off the shine without scuffing or darkening the leather much.
Baseball's rules require umpires to prepare the balls before each game, and teams' clubhouse staff rub dozens with the mud before every match.
MLB has tested alternatives, including balls with a tacky coating built in, but none has replaced the jar of riverbank mud.
